title: Gullwing logistics field capture
content:
Quick notes from field call with Gullwing Logistics (11/2025 cadence) — capture for follow-ups and handoff to ENG.

Context:
- Customer: Gullwing Logistics (regional 3PL + robotics operators). Running ~200 autonomous pallet movers, warehouse voice/UI for picks, and a dispatch planner service. Interested in hybrid approach: private deployment for PII/order payloads + hosted fallback for model experimentation.
- Goal: reduce operator cognitive load (natural language QA, exception handling), faster dispatch reroutes, and human-in-the-loop summarization for shift handoffs.
- Engagement stage: technical scoping and on-prem pilot (4 week PoC -> pilot -> prod).

What we heard (call 2025-11-08, 11:00 PT):
- Primary constraint: network connecting on-floor edge gateways to datacenter has intermittent spikes (20–90s windows) and occasional asymmetric NAT. They prefer local inference for safety-critical flows (door open confirmations, emergency stop translations).
- Compliance: orders include partial PII (customer phone/email). They require no egress of order-level payloads outside EU data center for those customers.
- Throughput profile: bursts of short requests at shift change (2–4k requests over 30s), otherwise steady low qps. Typical prompt length ~ 30–80 tokens; occasional long summarization (1–2k tokens) for end-of-shift reports.
- Latency tolerance: operator UI needs end-to-end <200ms for quick prompts; planning/dispatch can tolerate 500–800ms (async OK).
- Hardware: local DC has 2x A10 GPUs (shared across apps) and several CPU-only edge gateways (Xeon). They can provision 1x A100 if needed but procurement timeline ~8–10 weeks.

Technical requirements (explicit):
- Private deployment (VPC) with customer-managed control plane access (API endpoints in their DC).
- KMS integration for encryption at rest (YubiHSM available).
- Offline/air-gapped option for emergency mode — minimal image set & pre-pulled model artifacts.
- Model pinning and deterministic rollbacks for safety-critical flows.
- Token-level cost telemetry for finance (per-route metrics).

Potential design decisions discussed:
- Routing: keep safety-critical prompts local (private) and route experimental/LLM-heavy summarizers to hosted Redwood where allowed. Need a policy engine (by tag/route) with automatic fallback to lightweight model variant if local capacity exhausted.
- Caching: prefix/KV caching could cut costs for repeated confirmation phrasing — recommend customer-provided small persistent cache on local SSD to survive restarts.
- Quantization: run 4-bit quantized variant on A10 for cost. Validate quality on their prompt set (we should schedule an eval).
- Batching: prefer continuous batching with latency SLO; use small max batch windows (5–15ms) given operator latency requirement.

Gotchas & risks (field-observed):
- Networking: asymmetric NAT and MTU mismatch on one gateway cluster caused large websocket stall during demo last week. Action: SRE should validate keep-alive settings and websocket fragmentation.
- GPU drivers: their DC currently on CUDA 11.4; some of our optimized kernels require CUDA 12.* for best perf with A100. Fall back to CPU/less-optimized kernel may increase latency beyond SLO.
- Model size vs memory: A10 has limited VRAM for big-context summarization; multi-stage approach (local short-context + offload long summaries to hosted) necessary unless they add A100.
- Data classification: customer classification of PII is inconsistent across teams — need concrete examples of what must never leave local DC.

Preliminary perf/cost sketch (back-of-envelope):
- Short prompts (30–80 tokens): 90th p99 latency estimate on A10 quantized model ~110–160ms (with tuned kernels).
- Long summaries (1–2k tokens): local will be costly; propose async job to hosted fallback (post-processed) or run on A100. Estimated token cost if hosted used: ~€0.03 per 1k tokens (placeholder) — needs finance check.

Open questions to resolve (assign and timeline):
1) Definitive PII examples & tagging policy — Owner: Gullwing security (Elena K.) + Samira — due 2025-11-20.
2) Confirm if procurement can move up for 1x A100 (target Q1 2026) — Owner: Diego to confirm with infra contact (Marco) — due 2025-11-15.
3) Validate CUDA/driver compatibility matrix on staging nodes — Owner: Riley Chen (SRE) — run compatibility test this sprint (by 2025-11-12).
4) Short prompt eval with quantized variant (quality regression checks) — Owner: Aisha Nwosu (Applied ML) — dataset from Gullwing SHIFT logs; need sample by 2025-11-13.

Action items (next 2 weeks):
- [Samira] Draft non-production network config snippet for them (NAT traversal notes + websocket keepalive recommendations) — due 11/10.
- [Diego] Create RL ticket for on-prem private deployment template for A10/A100 fallback (RL-4782 created).
- [Aisha] Run quick eval (10–20 prompt pairs) of quantized model and share quality notes in PR (link below) — due 11/14.
- [Riley] Schedule short SRE session with Gullwing network team to reproduce MTU/NAT issue — 30m slot next week.
- [Gullwing:Elena] Provide redacted examples of PII and acceptable de-identification scheme — due 11/20.

Notes to self / informal thoughts:
- Consider shipping small policy engine config that matches their tag-based routing. Keep policy expressed as text file so security can audit easily.
- For emergency air-gap: make a minimal OCI bundle that contains runtime + quantized model and a small static HTML admin page to trigger fallback operations. Could pre-seed cache with last 24h transcripts.
- If they push A100 procurement, re-evaluate running long-summary models locally — may save cost and latency.

References / links used during call:
- internal demo recording: https://redwood.internal/meetings/gullwing-2025-11-08
- pilot brief template (confluence): https://redwood-confluence.internal/display/PILOT/Onprem+template
- draft PR for quant kernels: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rt-runtime/pull/642

Meeting wrap / suggested high-level next email to Gullwing:
- Reiterate: we’ll scope a 4-week PoC focused on operator UI flows (local-only for safety prompts) with a hosted async path for long summaries. Deliverables: pilot plan, driver/cuda checklist, small eval report on quantized model quality, and a network config snippet.
- Propose a follow-up call after we validate driver compat and receive PII examples (target: 11/21).

Last edited 2026-02-21: added follow-up notes after SRE repro attempt and updated CUDA compatibility status (staging nodes now show CUDA 12.1 available).
